land.text: Byzantine Sicily, taken piecemeal from the landing at Mazara in June 827 to Taormina on 1 August 902 and the last fortresses (Rometta) by 965

predecessors.note: The island was conquered over 75 years; the ledger dates every step the pages give. Cliopatria's Emirate row starts only in 850 and has no shape for 911-959 (that span lies inside the Fatimid Caliphate row).

land.text: Sicily, conquered by the Normans under Roger I from May 1061 to Noto in February 1091; the County of Sicily was created in 1071 (it became the Kingdom of Sicily in 1130, group eu-13 'kingdom-of-sicily')

successors.note: Malta fell later in 1091 (Mdina); the County page says the conquest of Malta was only completed in 1127.

capitals.name: Palermo
capitals.note: 'Palermo was conquered in 831 and became the new capital' (Kalbids page); the Emirate page names Palermo as the capital. From 827 to 830 the Muslims held only a landing ground at Mazara and no seat is recorded.

correction.text: the landing ground at Mazara in south-western Sicily and, after spring 828, Agrigento (undated on the page)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 827-830: Cliopatria has no shape before 850. The Aghlabid army landed at Mazara in June 827, besieged Syracuse in 827-828 without taking it, and after spring 828 'one part took Agrigento in the west' (undated). No infobox area exists to compare.

correction.text: Palermo (surrendered September 831) with the Mazara and Agrigento footholds

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 831-842: Palermo surrendered in September 831 and became the seat; Mazara and Agrigento held. Messina is not yet taken. The extent around the cities is the reading of the page (radii), not a surveyed border.

correction.text: the west with Palermo, Messina (843), Modica and Ragusa (845, 848) and Lentini (846)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 843-849: Messina taken 'in late 842 or 843' with Neapolitan support, Modica 845, Lentini 846, Ragusa 848. The ledger carries each step; the keyframe is the shape at the end of the period.

correction.text: Cliopatria's western shape plus Messina, Modica/Ragusa, Lentini and Cefalu, the fortresses the page dates 843-857

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's 850 shape (20 cells, 6,282 km2) is the Palermo-Trapani-Agrigento west only; it lacks Messina (843), Modica (845), Lentini (846), Ragusa (848) and Cefalu (857), all of which the page dates before 850-859 ends. Corrected to add them; no infobox area to compare.

Enna fell in January 859; 'The fall of Enna reduced the Byzantines to the eastern coastal strip between Syracuse and Taormina.' The 18,935 km2 shape (about three quarters of the island) fits that statement.
+470 km2 over the 860 shape (2.5 percent); the pages opened date no change between 859 and 870, so the shape stands as Cliopatria's small adjustment of the same frontier.
Malta (Melite) fell on 29 August 870; the shape's bounding box reaches 35.77 N and takes in Malta, as the page requires.

correction.text: the 878 shape without Taormina, which fell on 1 August 902 (the correction holds 878-901)

keyframe_review.note: Syracuse was stormed on 21 May 878, which the shape includes. But Taormina held out until 1 August 902 and the north-east (Val Demone) was the last to fall, while the shape holds the Taormina cell from 878. For 878-901 the shape should lack Taormina; from 902 it stands as drawn.

correction.text: Sicily as in the 960 shape, with Malta, under Fatimid governors (909-948) and then the Kalbid emirs

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 911-959: Cliopatria has no Emirate shape for these years; its Fatimid Caliphate row (911-1176) includes Sicily. The Emirate page shows one entity: Aghlabid province 827-909, Fatimid province 909-948, Kalbid autonomous emirate 948-1044. The island less the north-east strongholds that held until 965 is drawn here; the Fatimid dossier should drop Sicily from its 911-959 shapes.

Right for 960-1060 except that Malta, which Cliopatria drops after 910, was still Muslim: the Emirate page puts the fall of 'the island of Malta' in 1091, and the Muslim conquest page its capture in 870. Years 1061-1065 are replaced by the next keyframe (Messina lost). The 13 cells of the north-east left out are the Byzantine strongholds (Rometta) that held to 965.

correction.text: Sicily less the Messina-Taormina strip, with Malta

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1061-1065: Robert and Roger invaded in May 1061 and besieged Messina, 'the first permanent Norman conquest' (County page); Cliopatria shows the loss only in 1066. Drawn as the 1066 shape with Malta.
The 1066 shape (the island without the north-east strip) is consistent with the Norman hold on Messina from 1061 and Catania in 1071, but omits Malta.

Palermo fell on 10 January 1072 after a five-month siege (Emirate page; the Norman-conquest page says the Normans entered it on 7 January), which the shape shows. The interior and west (Trapani, Agrigento, Enna) are not dated by the pages opened: unverified: page budget. Malta added.

correction.text: Syracuse and Noto, with Malta, for 1085

keyframe_review.note: Syracuse's siege began in 1085 and it capitulated in March 1086, 'only Noto was still under Saracen dominion'; Noto fell in February 1091. The shape (Syracuse and Noto, 1,289 km2) is right for 1085; from 1086 it should lose Syracuse (next keyframe) and Cliopatria's end year 1093 should be 1091. Malta added.

correction.text: Noto at the south-eastern tip of Sicily and Malta

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1086-1090: after Syracuse capitulated in March 1086 'only Noto was still under Saracen dominion', and Malta (Mdina) was subdued only in 1091.

region.text: Mazara in south-western Sicily, where the Aghlabid army landed

ledger.note: 827: the Aghlabids land at Mazara. 'after three days they reached Mazara in southwestern Sicily, where they landed'; the page dates the departure from Sousse to 14 June 827 (the Emirate page puts the first battle on 15 July 827). The infobox of the Emirate page gives 827-1091.

region.text: Byzantine Sicily outside the western holdings: Enna, Syracuse and the east

ledger.note: 827: the war for the island opens. Syracuse was besieged in 827-828 but not taken; zone is the island outside Cliopatria's 850 shape.

region.text: Agrigento in the west

ledger.note: Spring 828 on: the page says only 'one part took Agrigento in the west' after the siege of Syracuse was lifted in spring 828; no year is given for Agrigento (828 is inferred).
831: Palermo becomes the capital: 'Palermo was conquered in 831 and became the new capital'.

region.text: Palermo and its district

ledger.note: 831: Palermo surrenders. 'until September 831, when its commander, the spatharios Symeon, surrendered it'; the first Aghlabid governor (wali) arrived there in March 832.

region.text: Messina and its strait

ledger.note: 842/843: Messina falls to the Muslims with Neapolitan support. 'In late 842 or 843, with Neapolitan support, the Muslims conquered Messina' (the Emirate page: 'in 842 or 843').

region.text: the fortress of Modica, in the south-east

ledger.note: 845: Modica falls. 'In 845, the fortress of Modica also fell.'

region.text: Leontini (Lentini)

ledger.note: 846: Lentini taken by a ruse. 'al-Fadl ibn Ja'far took Leontini by a ruse in 846.'

region.text: the fortress of Ragusa

ledger.note: 848: Ragusa surrenders. 'the fortress of Ragusa followed in 848, when its garrison was forced by severe famine to surrender.'

region.text: Cefalu on the northern coast

ledger.note: 857: Cefalu taken. 'Abbas captured several fortresses, including Cefalù in 857.'

region.text: Byzantine Sicily outside the western holdings

ledger.note: January 859: Enna falls; the contested ground narrows to the eastern strip (next contest).

region.text: Enna, 'the main Byzantine bulwark', and the interior

ledger.note: January 859: Enna taken. 'Then, in January 859, the Muslims scored a major success through the capture' of Enna; 'The fall of Enna reduced the Byzantines to the eastern coastal strip between Syracuse and Taormina.'

region.text: the eastern coastal strip between Syracuse and Taormina

ledger.note: 859-878: the Byzantine remnant is the strip from Syracuse to Taormina.

region.text: the island of Malta (Melite)

ledger.note: 29 August 870: Malta falls. 'the capital Melite fell on 29 August' (the page places this in 870).

region.text: Syracuse, the old Byzantine capital of the island

ledger.note: 21 May 878: Syracuse falls. 'finally, on 21 May 878, stormed the city.'

region.text: the eastern coastal strip between Syracuse and Taormina

ledger.note: 878: Syracuse taken; Taormina and the north-east (Val Demone) remain (next contest).

region.text: Taormina and the north-east (Val Demone), the last Christian strongholds

ledger.note: 878-965: Christian strongholds survived in 'the northeastern third of the island (Val Demone), which was the last to fall'.

region.text: Taormina on the north-east coast

ledger.note: 1 August 902: Taormina falls. 'the town fell on 1 August' (902); the infobox of the Muslim conquest ends 'June 827 – August 902'.
909: the Fatimids replace the Aghlabids. 'overthrown and replaced by the Shiite Fatimids' (909); Sicily is a Fatimid province 909-948. Same state, same colour (rule 2).

948: the Kalbid dynasty. 'After successfully suppressing a revolt the Fatimid caliph appointed al-Hasan al-Kalbi (948-953) as Emir of Sicily.' Same state. Infobox: 'Kalbid autonomous emirate (948-1044)'; the Kalbids page: 'formally appointed by the Fatimids, but gained, progressively, de facto autonomous rule'. After 1044 the island 'devolved into four qadits, or small fiefdoms' (Emirate page) and the Kalbids 'died out in 1053'; the fiefdoms have no dossiers and the shape stays one colour.

region.text: Taormina and the north-east (Val Demone)

ledger.note: 965: the last Byzantine fortresses on the island fall or are cleared. 'Isolated fortresses remained in Byzantine hands until 965' (the Rometta attack is undated on the Muslim conquest page; the Kalbids page: a Byzantine offensive 'crushed in 965 at the Battle of the Ditch or Rametta'). A lasting truce followed in 967.

region.text: Sicily, from Messina

ledger.note: May 1061: the Normans invade. 'Robert and Roger first invaded Sicily in May 1061'.

region.text: Messina, the first permanent Norman conquest

ledger.note: 1061: Messina is lost. 'In 1061 the first permanent Norman conquest'; the Norman-conquest page has them besiege Messina. The page does not say 'Messina' in the same sentence as the year.

region.text: Catania and the east coast

ledger.note: 1071: Catania falls. 'Catania fell to the Normans in 1071'; the County of Sicily was founded in 1071.

region.text: Palermo, the capital, and the northern coast

ledger.note: 10 January 1072: Palermo falls. 'would in turn fall on 10 January 1072 after a five-month siege' (the Norman-conquest page: 'entered by the Normans on 7 January 1072').

region.text: the interior and the west (Enna, Agrigento, Trapani, Mazara) between 1072 and 1086

ledger.note: By March 1086 only Noto was Saracen apart from Syracuse; the pages opened give no dates for Trapani, Agrigento or Enna. Placed at 1085, where Cliopatria shows the collapse; the bound 'when the city capitulated in March 1086 only Noto was still under Saracen dominion' is the page's.

region.text: Syracuse

ledger.note: March 1086: Syracuse capitulates. 'The siege began in 1085'; 'when the city capitulated in March 1086 only Noto was still under Saracen dominion.'

region.text: the island of Malta, the walled city of Mdina

ledger.note: 1091: Malta is lost. 'In 1091, Roger invaded Malta and subdued the walled city of Mdina'; the County page adds that its conquest was 'completed in 1127 when the Arab administration of the island was expelled'.

region.text: Noto at the south-eastern tip

ledger.note: February 1091: Noto yields. 'In February 1091 Noto yielded as well'; the County page: 'In February 1091 the conquest of Sicily was completed when Noto fell.'

region.text: Sicily

ledger.note: February 1091: the fighting ends with the fall of Noto.

region.text: Noto and Malta, the last holdings

ledger.note: February 1091: the Emirate ends. Noto, the last Muslim town on Sicily, yields to Count Roger; the Emirate page gives 827-1091. Cliopatria's last shape runs to 1093.

wars.name: Muslim conquest of Sicily
wars.outcome: Aghlabid victory in stages: Palermo 831, Messina 842/843, Enna January 859, Syracuse 21 May 878, Taormina 1 August 902; isolated fortresses held until 965 and a lasting truce was made in 967.
wars.note: The page's infobox gives June 827 - August 902. Malta fell on 29 August 870.

wars.name: Byzantine expedition to Sicily under George Maniakes
wars.outcome: The Emirate page gives a Byzantine crossing of the strait of Messina under George Maniaces in 1038 and 'another decisive victory in the summer of 1040'; it gives no territorial result in the passage read, so no zone is drawn.
wars.note: End year of the expedition not given by the page; 1040 is the last date it names. The Cliopatria shape 960-1065 shows no change.

wars.name: Norman conquest of Sicily

zones.text: Sicily, Messina in 1061 to Noto in 1091

wars.outcome: Norman victory: Messina 1061, Catania 1071, Palermo 10 January 1072, Syracuse March 1086, Noto February 1091; Malta invaded in 1091.
wars.note: The County of Sicily was created in 1071 for Roger Bosso.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey fixes any frontier: holdings were towns and fortresses taken one by one, the Val Demone strip and later the Norman-held north-east were never drawn as lines. Only the island's coast is firm.

sources.title: Emirate of Sicily
sources.note: Infobox 827-1091 (no area or capital given), Aghlabid/Fatimid/Kalbid status, Palermo 10 January 1072, Syracuse 1086, Noto and Malta 1091, the four qadits in 1044, Maniakes 1038-1040.

sources.title: Muslim conquest of Sicily
sources.note: The conquest year by year, 827-902: Mazara, Palermo 831, Messina 842/843, Modica, Lentini, Ragusa, Cefalu, Enna 859, Malta 29 August 870, Syracuse 21 May 878, Taormina 1 August 902, fortresses to 965.

sources.title: County of Sicily
sources.note: The Norman county: 1061 first permanent conquest, 1071 foundation, Noto February 1091, Malta 1091-1127, Palermo capital. Thin on 1063-1090.

sources.title: Norman conquest of southern Italy
sources.note: Sicily 1061-1091: May 1061 invasion, Palermo 7 January 1072, Syracuse March 1086, Noto February 1091, Malta 1091.

sources.title: Kalbids
sources.note: 948 appointment of al-Hasan al-Kalbi, de facto autonomy, Palermo capital from 831, 965 battle, Hasan as-Samsam 1040-1053, dynasty dies out 1053.

notes: Page budget (5) fully used. No infobox area on any page, so the area comparison could not be made. Cliopatria rows: no Emirate shape for 911-959 (Sicily lies inside the Fatimid Caliphate row 911-1176, which should drop it); Malta drops out of the Emirate shapes after 910 although the pages put its fall in 1091; the 1085 shape runs to 1093 but Noto fell in February 1091. The collapse of the interior between 1072 and 1086 (Trapani, Agrigento, Enna, Mazara) is undated on the pages opened: confidence 1. The Aghlabid and Fatimid province phases and the Kalbid autonomy (948-1044) are recorded as rename events here, not as vassalage: vassal_start/vassal_end belong to the suzerain, so the Fatimid dossier should carry a vassal_start in 948 (counterpart emirate-of-sicily) and a vassal_end in 1044 on the Emirate page's 'Kalbid autonomous emirate (948-1044)'. The mainland Aghlabid emirates (Bari 847-871, Taranto 839-880) are not on any page opened and are not in this dossier. Place names not in the gazetteer on 2026-10-25: Mazara del Vallo, Agrigento (as a place), Lentini, Cefalu, Taormina; Enna was not found. County of Sicily (1071-1130) has no dossier of its own; it is within norman-italy then kingdom-of-sicily.
